strings.name: Shakira
strings.summary: Shakira developed from a teenage Colombian singer into a pop musician working across languages, combining rock, Latin rhythms and dance. Albums including Pies Descalzos and Laundry Service, and songs such as “Waka Waka,” expanded her international audience. She has also supported children’s education through her foundation and UNICEF. Outside her musical career, she reached a plea agreement in a Spanish tax case in 2023, accepting a suspended sentence and fines.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to the May 2026 Rio performance. The two tax cases are distinguished; future tour reports are not treated as completed events.
strings.influence.rationale: Combined Latin, rock and pop music to reach audiences across languages, while supporting Colombian children's education through her charitable foundation.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Music across languages
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Through Laundry Service and songs including “Hips Don’t Lie,” expanded Latin pop audiences across Spanish- and English-language markets.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Sustained work for children’s education
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Supported schooling and early development through the Pies Descalzos Foundation and UNICEF activities.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Performs a free show on Copacabana Beach
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Presented songs from her career at Rio de Janeiro’s Todo Mundo no Rio event, a free beach concert.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran wins a Grammy
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The album won Best Latin Pop Album, marking an important recognition of this phase of recording and touring.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: A separate tax investigation is dismissed
strings.timeline.event-03.text: A Spanish court closed a separate investigation concerning 2018 taxes; it was distinct from the case settled in 2023.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Releases Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Released her first studio album in seven years, bringing together collaborations and new songs from a period of personal change.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Reaches an agreement in a Spanish tax case
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Accepted a plea agreement over taxes from 2012–2014, receiving a three-year suspended sentence and fines rather than proceeding with trial.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Co-headlines the Super Bowl halftime show
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Performed with Jennifer Lopez, bringing Latin music, dance and their respective songs to a major televised sporting event.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Creates a World Cup official song
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Collaborated with South African band Freshlyground on “Waka Waka,” the World Cup’s official song, and performed it at the closing ceremony.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: “Hips Don’t Lie” expands her international reach
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Her collaboration with Wyclef Jean combined Latin rhythms, pop and dance, becoming a representative work of her cross-language career.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Appointed a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Began supporting children’s rights and education as a Goodwill Ambassador, extending her advocacy through international institutional work.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Releases Laundry Service
strings.timeline.event-10.text: The mainly English-language album included “Whenever, Wherever,” opening a broader phase of work across languages.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Breaks through with Pies Descalzos
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Her third album brought a stronger rock and songwriting approach, gradually expanding her audience in Latin America and Spain.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Releases Magia as a teenager
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Released her debut after signing with Sony’s Colombian division, including songs she had begun writing in childhood.
strings.timeline.event-13.title: Born in Barranquilla
strings.timeline.event-13.text: Born in the Colombian Caribbean city of Barranquilla; began writing, singing and dancing as a child.
